_comment: Per-wave ledger. Slow-moving and human-curated. The volatile cumulative counters live in incident.json and are owned by the refresh schedule. Nothing enters this file without a named claimant.

waves.label: Wave one
waves.btcQualifier: first reported at 594 BTC in a 25-minute sweep, revised past 1,000
waves.topologyText: Shared collection wallets — a handful of destinations, trivially clusterable.
waves.claimedBy: Block — Bitcoin Engineering and Security teams

waves.label: Wave two
waves.btcQualifier: not disclosed separately; folded into the 1,367 BTC cumulative by 2 August
waves.topologyText: Shared collection wallets, same pattern as wave one.

waves.label: Wave three
waves.btcQualifier: cumulative reached 1,367 BTC across 4,585 addresses at the close of this wave
waves.topologyText: Shared collection wallets. This is the last wave that clusters cleanly.

waves.label: Wave four
waves.btcQualifier: 388.93 BTC confirmed across 218 transactions from 462 addresses, revised to ~448.73 BTC across 709 addresses
waves.rate: 13.8 sweeps per block · roughly 45x the prior rate
waves.topologyText: Freshly generated addresses, one per victim, with no prior history. The clustering that worked on waves one to three does not work here.
waves.rbfText: Sweeps were broadcast with replace-by-fee opt-in and sat unconfirmed in the mempool. A victim who noticed in time could broadcast a conflicting transaction spending the same UTXOs to an address they still controlled, at a higher fee rate, and win the race. It is the only point in this whole incident where the defender had a move.
waves.claimedBy: Galaxy Research — Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research

actors.text: Wave four's fragmented topology differs from the earlier waves in a way that points to independent operators racing the same disclosure rather than one coordinated group finishing a job. Reporting describes multiple groups moving across the vulnerable set in parallel.

custody.text: Roughly three quarters of the take has not moved since it landed. The remainder has left its first destination. No tier-1 or tier-2 source has published a named address set for wave four, so where it went is not stated here — and because wave four used one fresh address per victim rather than shared collectors, an apparent 'movement' signal can be topology rather than a cash-out. Treat the split as reported, not as verified.

sourceTiers.1: On-chain and self-verifiable. Block heights, timestamps, confirmations, fee rates — read live from mempool.space and checkable by anyone against any node. Requires trusting no one.
sourceTiers.2: Named attribution research. A named analyst or firm doing the address clustering: Galaxy Research, Block's security teams, ZachXBT, Chainalysis, Elliptic. This tier decides WHICH addresses belong to the attack, which a block explorer cannot tell you.
sourceTiers.3: Vendor statement. Coinkite's own advisories on scope and remediation.
sourceTiers.4: Press aggregating tiers 2 and 3. Citable, but the figure belongs to whoever the outlet is quoting, and that name is what gets recorded here.
sourceTiers.5: Unattributed social posts. Never written into these files. Used only as a lead to chase into tier 1 or tier 2.

rule: No figure is published without a named claimant. Where a claim cannot be raised above tier 5, the prior value stands and the discrepancy is recorded in the unverified list rather than shown as a number.
